solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Explorer books taxi to the west (5)

indicatorNotes.to the west: in an across answer west is the left, so CAB goes before the books

blocks.note: OT = Old Testament, a set of books

annotation.surface: An explorer hails a cab and heads west with his books.
annotation.walkthrough: John Cabot sailed from Bristol to North America in 1497. The clue lists books before taxi, but 'to the west' puts the taxi first.
annotation.definitionFit: John Cabot was the Venetian explorer who reached Newfoundland for England.

entries.clue: Company accountant’s heading fraudulent racket (9)

indicatorNotes.heading: the accountant's letters head, or go in front of, the company's

annotation.surface: A company's accountant is at the head of a fraudulent racket.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Racket' looks like a scam to go with 'fraudulent', but here it is noise. CA is the British chartered accountant.
annotation.definitionFit: A cacophony is a harsh, discordant din, which is what a racket is.

entries.clue: Harry seen half-cut in punt (5)

indicatorNotes.half-cut: SEEN is cut in half, keeping SE
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places SE within the word for punt, so BET holds it

annotation.surface: Harry has been spotted drunk ('half-cut') out on a punt.
annotation.walkthrough: Harry is a verb, not a name, and half-cut is British slang for tipsy; here it just halves SEEN. A punt is a bet as well as a flat-bottomed boat.
annotation.definitionFit: To harry is to harass persistently, as troubles beset someone.

entries.clue: Sad short story enthralling guy in charge (8)

indicatorNotes.short: 'short' means lacking its end, so the word for story loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.enthralling: to enthral is to hold captive, so TAL holds RAG and IC inside it

blocks.note: to guy is to tease or rag

annotation.surface: A sad little tale grips a man who is in charge of something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Guy' is a verb meaning to mock, so it gives RAG rather than a man.
annotation.definitionFit: Tragical is an old or literary form of tragic, meaning sad.

entries.clue: Closest friend caging writer like an animal (9)

indicatorNotes.caging: BEST ALLY shuts I in, as a cage holds an animal

blocks.note: the writer of the clue calls himself I

annotation.surface: Your best friend keeps a writer caged like a zoo animal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Caging' fits the animal of the definition, but here it only tells you to put one letter inside the phrase. The writer is I, the setter speaking of himself.
annotation.definitionFit: Bestially means in the manner of a beast, like an animal.

entries.clue: Slight problem of male falling out of balloon (4)

indicatorNotes.falling out of: something falling out of a container is no longer in it, so the male letter leaves the balloon

blocks.note: a blimp is an airship, a gas balloon

annotation.surface: A man falls out of a hot-air balloon, which is more than a slight problem.
annotation.walkthrough: The understatement is the joke: a man falling from a balloon is hardly a blip.
annotation.definitionFit: A blip is a minor, temporary setback.

entries.clue: A little knowledge is ultimately of importance (10)

annotation.surface: A proverb-like line: even a little knowledge matters in the end.
annotation.walkthrough: It echoes the saying 'a little knowledge is a dangerous thing', and 'is' looks like the verb joining the halves.
annotation.definitionFit: A smattering is a slight, superficial knowledge of a subject.

entries.clue: Run through one’s plans, initially over beer (6)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down answer, these letters sit above ALE

annotation.surface: Someone runs through their plans for the evening over a pint.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Run through' reads as rehearse, but it means pierce. 'One's' stands for 'one is', hence I'M.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the physical sense of 'run through', piercing with a blade or stake, not the rehearsing sense the surface uses.

entries.clue: Left furniture store, exhausted very quickly (4,1,4)

annotation.surface: Someone walks out of a furniture store worn out, as shoppers often do.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a verb, walked out, but it is only L.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: something done at the speed of a bullet leaving a gun happens instantly.

entries.clue: Ferment cored apples in still (5)

indicatorNotes.cored: APPLES has its core taken out, leaving A and S
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' puts the leftover apple letters within the word for still

annotation.surface: A cider-maker's tip: put cored apples into a still to ferment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Still' pulls towards distilling, but it is the adverb YET. Ferment is a noun here, the agent that causes fermentation.
annotation.definitionFit: The noun 'ferment' names any agent that causes fermentation, and the brewer's fungus is the standard example.

entries.clue: CIA tangled with Castro in part of Central America (5,4)

indicatorNotes.tangled with: the letters of CIA and CASTRO are tangled together

annotation.surface: Cold War history: the CIA tangling with Fidel Castro in Central America.
annotation.walkthrough: The history points to Cuba, which is in the Caribbean; the letters give its Central American neighbour.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the country lies between Nicaragua and Panama on the Central American isthmus.

entries.clue: Declared cockle kosher (5)

indicatorNotes.Declared: said out loud, so we want a word that sounds like the next one

blocks.note: to cockle is to wrinkle or pucker

annotation.surface: Someone announces that a cockle is kosher, which shellfish never is.
annotation.walkthrough: Cockle is a verb, as paper cockles when wet, not the shellfish. Pukka is Anglo-Indian slang, common in Britain, for genuine or proper.
annotation.definitionFit: Kosher in its loose sense means genuine or legitimate, as pukka does.

entries.clue: Groupspeak of Love Island, beyond glib (6)

indicatorNotes.beyond: 'beyond' means further along, so the Love Island letters come after the word for glib

blocks.note: a pat answer is a glib one
love = nil = O in tennis scores

annotation.surface: The jargon of Love Island, the British dating reality show, is worse than glib.
annotation.walkthrough: Love Island is a British TV dating show, so the words look like one title, but they are split into O and IS.
annotation.definitionFit: A patois is the dialect or jargon of a particular group.

entries.clue: Strong muscles suffering reverse growth (8)

indicatorNotes.suffering reverse: LATS suffer a reverse and turn round to STAL

blocks.note: a wart is a small growth on the skin

annotation.surface: Strong muscles that suffer a setback in their growth.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reverse growth' reads as one idea, shrinking, but 'reverse' belongs with the muscles.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word began as 'stalworth', sturdy and brave, and still describes someone physically strong or staunch.

entries.clue: Ringing shortly before the hour, interrupting senior Scot (10)

indicatorNotes.interrupting: TEN TO breaks into SR IAN, after the S

blocks.note: ten to the hour, as in 'ten to six'
Ian, a typically Scottish first name

annotation.surface: A phone rings just before the hour and interrupts an elderly Scotsman.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ringing' looks like a phone or bell, but it describes a loud voice. The time phrase splits the abbreviation for senior, not the Scot's name.
annotation.definitionFit: A stentorian voice is loud and ringing, after Stentor, the herald in the Iliad.

entries.clue: Spooner’s model blooms for great artists (3,7)

indicatorNotes.Spooner’s: Rev Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: a mould is a model or template; its opening M is handed to the next word
asters are daisy-like flowers; they take the M from the first word

annotation.surface: Spooner's model flowers are fit for great painters.
annotation.walkthrough: MOULD ASTERS becomes OLD MASTERS when the M moves from the front of the first word to the second.
annotation.definitionFit: A fixed term for the leading European painters from about 1300 to 1800, such as Rembrandt or Titian.

entries.clue: Simply drink punch (9)

blocks.note: to down a drink is to drink it
a right is a punch with the right hand

annotation.surface: Just have some punch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Punch' sits next to 'drink' as a bowl of punch, but it is a boxer's blow.
annotation.definitionFit: Downright as an adverb means utterly, simply, as in 'downright rude'.

entries.clue: Tough day finally ending (4)

annotation.surface: A hard day is at last over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tough' is an adjective in the surface but a noun in the answer: a tough is a thug.
annotation.definitionFit: A tough is a rough, violent man, a thug.

entries.clue: General Assembly greeted eccentric widget enthusiast? (9)

indicatorNotes.eccentric: GREETED is rearranged in an eccentric way

blocks.note: first letters of General Assembly, the UN's main body

annotation.surface: The UN General Assembly welcomes an eccentric gadget fan.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'widget enthusiast' defines by example: a widget is one kind of gadget.
annotation.definitionFit: A gadgeteer is someone who loves gadgets such as widgets.

entries.clue: Wrong about time going on forever (8)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' means around, so the word for wrong wraps round the time letter

annotation.surface: Someone is wrong about how long something will go on.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' reads as 'concerning', but it puts IMMORAL around T.
annotation.definitionFit: Something immortal lives or lasts forever.

entries.clue: Cry of unknown bird (4)

blocks.note: x, y and z are unknowns in algebra

annotation.surface: A strange cry comes from a bird no one can name.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unknown bird' looks like one phrase, but 'unknown' is the algebraic Y.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, usually for the long wail of a cat or dog.

entries.clue: Dull maiden aunt led astray (10)

indicatorNotes.led astray: the letters of MAIDEN AUNT wander into a new order

annotation.surface: A dull maiden aunt has been led astray, which would liven her up.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is that a dull maiden aunt led astray would stop being dull.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: without animation, so lacking life or spirit.

entries.clue: Effectively performing King Lear without crowns (2,4)

indicatorNotes.without crowns: each word loses its head, its first letter

annotation.surface: An actor performs King Lear well, even without the crown.
annotation.walkthrough: The crowns belong to the king in the surface; in the wordplay they are the first letters of both words.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from engines: once the gears engage, the machine drives properly, so a person 'in gear' is functioning well.

entries.clue: Don’t arm a lunatic arbitrarily (2,6)

indicatorNotes.lunatic: the letters of DON'T ARM A go mad

annotation.surface: Advice: don't hand a weapon to a madman at random.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lunatic' reads as a noun, the madman, but it is the anagram indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: At random means arbitrarily, without method.

entries.clue: See you pass on gold rings (5)

indicatorNotes.rings: AU forms a ring round DIE

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
to pass on is to die

annotation.surface: Someone says goodbye and passes on some gold rings.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pass on' reads as hand over, but it is the euphemism for die.
annotation.definitionFit: Adieu is a goodbye, like 'see you'.

entries.clue: Mate rising extremely late (6)

indicatorNotes.extremely: take the extremes, first and last letters, of LATE

blocks.note: a coup is a rising against a government

annotation.surface: A friend gets up very late.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rising' looks like getting out of bed, but it is a noun, an uprising. 'Mate' is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: animals that pair up to breed are said to couple.

entries.clue: Look happy at last after vegetable pasty (5)

indicatorNotes.at last: take the last letters of 'look' and 'happy'
indicatorNotes.after: 'after' means following, so these two letters come behind the vegetable

blocks.note: last letters of LOOK and HAPPY

annotation.surface: Someone looks pleased at last after eating a vegetable pasty.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pasty' reads as the Cornish pie, but it is the adjective, pale. Peaky is British for looking pale and unwell.
annotation.definitionFit: Peaky means pale and sickly-looking, which is what pasty means.

entries.clue: Picked up late fruit (4)

indicatorNotes.Picked up: heard, picked up by the ear

annotation.surface: Someone gathered some late fruit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' fits fruit-picking in the surface but signals a sound.
annotation.definitionFit: The sloe is the small sour fruit of the blackthorn.

entries.clue: Individuals lacking clothing and fire (5)

indicatorNotes.lacking clothing: SINGLES loses its outer letters, the clothes around it

blocks.note: SINGLES without its first and last S

annotation.surface: People without clothes huddle round a fire.
annotation.walkthrough: An ingle is a fire on a hearth, as in inglenook.
annotation.definitionFit: Ingle is a Scots and old word for a household fire.

entries.clue: Anxious, some vacillate as expected (3,2,4)

indicatorNotes.some: the answer is some of the letters of the next words

blocks.note: the letters run from the fourth letter of 'vacillate' to the first of 'expected'

annotation.surface: Anxious people tend to vacillate, as you'd expect.
annotation.walkthrough: The hidden answer spans three words, starting inside 'vacillate'.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone not at ease is uneasy, which is a milder way of saying anxious.

entries.clue: Mistakenly neuter cat, it’s said (9)

indicatorNotes.Mistakenly: the letters of NEUTER CAT are put in the wrong order

annotation.surface: Rumour has it that someone had the wrong cat neutered.
annotation.walkthrough: 'It's said' reads as 'rumour has it', but it is the definition: an utterance is something said.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic-leaning paraphrase: anything uttered is spoken, so 'it's said' describes the thing the answer names.
annotation.definitionNote: 'it's said' is a clause standing for the noun: an utterance is a thing that is said

entries.clue: Film hen? (5)

blocks.note: a film in the sense of a thin coating spread over a surface
a hen named for what she does: she produces eggs

annotation.walkthrough: 'Film hen' tempts you towards movies such as Chicken Run, but film here is a thin coating.
annotation.definitionFit: A layer is a thin coating, and also a hen that lays eggs.
